title: Finite presentation and rigidity of a fibre-injective source
statement: Let $A$ be a valuation ring, meaning an integral domain whose fraction field $K$ satisfies $a\in A$ or $a^{-1}\in A$ for every $a\in K^\times$, with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_A$. Let $A\to S$ be a local homomorphism of commutative local rings, meaning that the inverse image of the maximal ideal of $S$ is $\mathfrak m_A$. Assume that $S$ is essentially of finite presentation over $A$: it is a localization of a finitely presented $A$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Let $N,M$ be finite $S$-modules [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], and let $u:N\to M$ be $S$-linear. Suppose that $M$ is flat as an $A$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] and that $N/\mathfrak m_AN\to M/\mathfrak m_AM$ induced by $u$ is injective. For an $S$-module $L$, $\mathfrak m_A L$ denotes the submodule generated by products of elements of $\mathfrak m_A$ with elements of $L$. Then $N$ is finitely presented over $S$ [def-sc-finitely-presented-module]. In addition, for every finitely presented $S$-module $E$ and surjective $S$-linear map $v:E\twoheadrightarrow N$ for which $E/\mathfrak m_AE\to N/\mathfrak m_AN$ is an isomorphism, $v$ is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Write $S=W^{-1}P$ with $P$ a finitely presented $A$-algebra. Its finite presentation gives a surjection $A[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\twoheadrightarrow P$ [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], so $P$ is of finite type [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Thus $S$ is essentially of finite type over $A$ [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra].

source.place: Tag 0GSG (lemma-mod-injective-valuation-ring), proof, second and third reduction paragraphs, lines 5067--5090

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-valuation-flat-finite-module-presentation] to $A\to S$ and $M$. The base is a valuation ring, the map is local and essentially of finite type by Step 1, and $M$ is finite over $S$ and flat over $A$ by hypothesis. Hence $M$ is finitely presented over $S$.

source.place: Tag 0GSE (lemma-valuation-ring-flat-essentially-finite-type), part (2), as used in Tag 0GSG, final paragraph

proof.text: First prove the rigidity assertion without assuming $N$ finitely presented. Let $E,v$ satisfy its hypotheses and put $w=u\circ v:E\to M$. On the closed fibre, $\overline w=\overline u\circ\overline v$ is injective, since $\overline v$ is an isomorphism and $\overline u$ is injective. Apply [lem-trf-valuation-general-mod-injective] with base $A$, algebra $S$, source $E$, target $M$, and map $w$. Locality and essential finite presentation of $S$ are assumed; both modules are finitely presented by hypothesis and Step 2; the target is $A$-flat. It follows that $w$ is injective. If $v(e)=0$, then $w(e)=0$, so $e=0$. Therefore $v$ is bijective. Its inverse is $S$-linear, since uniqueness of preimages gives $v^{-1}(n+n')=v^{-1}(n)+v^{-1}(n')$ and $v^{-1}(sn)=sv^{-1}(n)$. This proves the second assertion.

source.place: Tag 0GSG (lemma-mod-injective-valuation-ring), proof, second and third reduction paragraphs, lines 5067--5090

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-valuation-finite-module-fp-reduction] to the local essentially finite type map $A\to S$ from Step 1 and the finite $S$-module $N$. Obtain a nonempty filtered system of finitely presented modules $N_\lambda$, with surjective transitions and colimit $N$, whose closed-fibre comparison maps are eventually isomorphisms. Every colimit map $v_\lambda:N_\lambda\to N$ is surjective: any element of this module colimit is represented by a finite sum of stage elements; take a common receiving stage for them and for $\lambda$, add their images there, and lift that sum through the surjective transition from $N_\lambda$. Choose a stage where $\overline v_\lambda$ is an isomorphism. Step 3 applies with $E=N_\lambda$, so $v_\lambda$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0GSG (lemma-mod-injective-valuation-ring), proof, second and third reduction paragraphs, lines 5067--5090

proof.text: Take a finite presentation $S^a\to S^b\xrightarrow{p}N_\lambda\to0$ [def-sc-finitely-presented-module]. The composite $v_\lambda p$ is surjective and has kernel $\ker p$, because $v_\lambda$ is bijective by Step 4. Thus $S^a\to S^b\xrightarrow{v_\lambda p}N\to0$ is exact, proving that $N$ is finitely presented over $S$.
